subject: Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting

questions.topic: Safety Rules and Regulations in Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: Which item of personal protective equipment is MOST important for a painter spraying a two-pack (2K) polyurethane paint containing isocyanate hardener?
questions.explanation: Isocyanate vapour and mist attack the lungs, so an air-fed respirator is required; a simple dust mask or other PPE does not protect the airways.

questions.topic: Safety Rules and Regulations in Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: Spilled engine oil on the floor of an auto body workshop in Ibadan should first be
options: washed away with plenty of water
wiped with a rag soaked in thinner
covered with sawdust or dry sand and swept up
questions.explanation: An absorbent such as sawdust or dry sand soaks up the oil so it can be swept up; water only spreads oil and thinner adds a fire hazard.

questions.topic: Safety Rules and Regulations in Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: Which of the following is a HUMAN factor that causes accidents in an auto body workshop?
questions.explanation: Horseplay is caused by the behaviour of people; the other options are machine or workshop-condition hazards.

questions.topic: Safety Rules and Regulations in Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: A solvent recovery system in a spray painting shop is used mainly to
options: increase the air pressure supplied to the spray gun
dry the paint film faster in the oven
reclaim used thinner for re-use and reduce hazardous waste
filter dust from the spray booth intake air
questions.explanation: Solvent recovery units distil dirty gun-wash thinner so it can be reused, cutting the amount of hazardous waste sent for disposal.

questions.stem: The hand tool held behind a dented panel while the panel is struck with a body hammer is the
questions.explanation: A dolly is the shaped steel block held against the back of the panel; spoons spread the blow or reach confined areas.

questions.stem: The portable hydraulic unit used to push or pull out damaged sections of a vehicle body is called a
questions.explanation: A body jack (porta-power) uses a pump, hose and ram with attachments to push or pull body sections; a trolley jack only lifts the vehicle.

questions.stem: Draining the water trap of the air compressor and checking the belt tension every week, before any fault occurs, is an example of
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance is planned, routine work done at fixed intervals to stop faults occurring; corrective maintenance repairs a fault after it occurs.

questions.stem: Monitoring the vibration and temperature of a compressor motor so that bearings are replaced just before they are likely to fail is known as
questions.explanation: Predictive maintenance uses condition measurements to forecast when a part will fail; preventive maintenance follows a fixed time schedule regardless of condition.

questions.topic: Materials for Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: Body solder described as 30/70 contains
questions.explanation: Body solder is a tin-lead alloy and the first figure is the tin content; the low tin content gives a long plastic range for wiping.

questions.topic: Materials for Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: A panel beater has 2.5 kg of 40/60 body solder. What mass of tin does it contain?
questions.explanation: 40/60 solder is 40% tin, so tin = 0.40 x 2.5 kg = 1.0 kg; 1.5 kg is the lead content.

questions.topic: Materials for Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: Which of the following is an UNDERCOAT rather than a top coat?
questions.explanation: Primers, putties, fillers and sealers form the undercoat system; lacquers, enamels and clear coats are top coats.

questions.topic: Materials for Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: A rivet that can be set from one side of a panel only, using a hand rivet gun, is a
questions.explanation: Pop or blind rivets are set from one side with a rivet gun; solid rivets need access to both sides for a dolly and set.

questions.stem: Which of these metals is NON-FERROUS?
questions.explanation: Non-ferrous metals contain no iron as the main constituent; mild steel, cast iron and carbon steel are all iron-based.

questions.stem: The property that allows mild steel sheet to be hammered and rolled into a new shape without cracking is
questions.explanation: Malleability is the ability to be deformed by hammering or rolling; ductility is the ability to be drawn into wire.

questions.stem: Most outer body panels of mass-produced Nigerian-assembled and imported cars are made from
questions.explanation: Low-carbon steel sheet is cheap, easily pressed and weldable, so it is the usual panel material; cast iron and tool steel are too brittle or hard.

questions.stem: Heating steel to the correct temperature and then cooling it very slowly inside the furnace is called
questions.explanation: Slow furnace cooling (annealing) softens the steel and relieves stress; quenching is rapid cooling used in hardening.

questions.stem: Hardened steel is reheated to a temperature below its critical range and cooled in order to
options: reduce brittleness while keeping most of the hardness
make it as soft as possible
increase its grain size for machining
questions.explanation: This is tempering, which trades a little hardness for toughness; adding carbon to the surface is case-hardening.

questions.stem: Which heat treatment gives a low-carbon steel part a hard, wear-resistant outer skin while its core stays tough?
questions.explanation: Case-hardening (e.g. carburising) adds carbon to the surface layer which is then hardened; low-carbon steel cannot be through-hardened.

questions.stem: An oxy-acetylene flame burning equal volumes of oxygen and acetylene is called a
questions.explanation: Equal volumes give the neutral flame used for most steel welding; excess acetylene gives a carburising (reducing) flame and excess oxygen an oxidising flame.

questions.stem: Free acetylene should not be used at a working pressure above about
questions.explanation: Above about 1 bar (15 psi) free acetylene can decompose explosively, so regulators are never set higher.

questions.stem: The device fitted at the regulator or torch to stop a flame travelling back into the hose and cylinder is the
questions.explanation: A flashback arrestor contains a flame barrier and a non-return valve; gauges only show pressure.

questions.stem: Small gas holes found throughout an oxy-acetylene weld after cutting it open are MOST likely caused by
options: welding over rust, paint or moisture on the joint
questions.explanation: Porosity is gas trapped in the solidifying metal, usually from contamination such as rust, paint, oil or moisture; clean the joint to remedy it.

questions.stem: A vehicle body in which the floor pan, pillars and panels are welded together to form one load-carrying unit without a separate chassis frame is
questions.explanation: In an integral body the shell carries the loads; a composite body is bolted onto a separate chassis frame.

questions.stem: When the hammer strikes the panel directly over the dolly, the metal is
questions.explanation: Hammer-on-dolly squeezes the metal between hammer and dolly, which stretches it; hammer-off-dolly is used to raise low spots with little stretching.

questions.stem: In heat-shrinking an over-stretched panel, a small spot is heated to cherry red and then
options: tapped down with a hammer and dolly and quenched with a wet rag
left to cool slowly and filled with putty
questions.explanation: The heated spot upsets (thickens) as it is tapped and contracts as it is quenched, drawing the stretched metal back.

questions.stem: The three main body sections of a car are the front (engine) section, the centre section and the
questions.explanation: Bodies are divided into front, centre (passenger) and rear sections for damage assessment and repair.

questions.stem: In major collision repair, the basic alignment principle is that the body must be measured and pulled back so that
options: the doors close regardless of measurements
the damaged panels are replaced first before measuring
reference points match the manufacturer's dimensions in length, width and height
questions.explanation: Alignment uses datum (height), centreline (width) and zero planes (length) to bring reference points back to the specified dimensions before panels are fitted.

questions.stem: Aluminium panels need extra care during repair because aluminium
options: is harder than steel and cannot be bent
work-hardens quickly and gives no colour change before it melts
questions.explanation: Aluminium hardens and cracks if overworked and does not glow before melting, so heat must be controlled with crayons or a thermometer.

questions.stem: Separate tools and sanding discs are kept for aluminium repair work mainly to prevent
options: steel particles being embedded and causing galvanic corrosion
paint from sticking to the panel
questions.explanation: Steel particles in contact with aluminium set up galvanic corrosion under the paint, so tools are kept separate.

questions.stem: A plastic that softens each time it is heated and can therefore be repaired by melting (welding) is
questions.explanation: Thermoplastics such as polypropylene and ABS remelt on heating; thermosetting plastics char instead of melting.

questions.stem: Before welding a cracked plastic bumper, the repairer must first
options: identify the type of plastic so that a matching welding rod is used
heat the whole bumper to soften it
apply a coat of primer over the crack
fill the crack with body solder
questions.explanation: Plastic welds only fuse if the rod is the same plastic as the part, usually identified from the moulded code (e.g. PP, ABS).

questions.stem: A glass fibre panel repair uses glass fibre mat with
questions.explanation: The mat is wetted with catalysed polyester (or epoxy) resin which sets into a rigid laminate.

questions.stem: A spray gun with its paint cup mounted on TOP of the gun body is a
questions.explanation: Paint flows down from a top cup by gravity; a siphon gun has the cup underneath and a pressure-feed gun uses a separate pressurised pot.

questions.stem: The part of the spray gun that atomises the paint and controls the shape of the spray fan is the
questions.explanation: Air jets from the air cap break the paint into droplets and its horns shape the fan; the trigger only opens the air and fluid valves.

questions.stem: Small craters with a raised rim appearing in fresh top coat ("fish-eyes") are MOST often caused by
options: silicone or wax contamination not removed during surface preparation
too much hardener in the paint
questions.explanation: Silicone or wax on the surface repels paint; cleaning with a wax and grease remover before painting prevents fish-eyes.

questions.stem: The main reason for using the manufacturer's paint code when ordering paint for a repair is to
options: find the price of the paint
know the thickness of the steel
obtain the exact colour and paint type originally used on the vehicle
determine the age of the driver
questions.explanation: The paint code (found on the vehicle identification plate) gives the formula for the original colour, so the repair matches.

questions.stem: When spraying metallic paint, applying the coat WETTER (heavier and closer) than normal tends to make the colour
questions.explanation: In a wet film the aluminium flakes sink and lie at random so less light is reflected, giving a darker shade; a dry application looks lighter.

questions.stem: Which factor is LEAST important when choosing a location for a new auto body repair shop in Onitsha?
options: The colour of the neighbouring buildings
questions.explanation: Access, land cost, power and capital determine whether the shop can operate; neighbouring building colour has no effect.

questions.stem: For a respray of one door, a workshop spends ₦3,500 on filler, ₦18,000 on paint, ₦4,000 on abrasives and masking materials and ₦25,000 on labour. If it adds 20% profit to the total cost, what should it charge?
questions.explanation: Total cost = ₦50,500; 20% profit = ₦10,100; charge = ₦60,600.

questions.stem: A two-pack top coat is mixed in the ratio 4 : 1 : 1 (paint : hardener : thinner). How much paint is needed to make 1.5 litres of ready-to-spray mixture?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 6; paint = 4/6 x 1.5 L = 1.0 L, with 0.25 L each of hardener and thinner.

questions.topic: Safety Rules and Regulations in Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of safety rules and regulations in an auto body repair and spray painting workshop. [2 marks]
(b) List four items of personal protective equipment used in the workshop and state what each protects. [8 marks]
(c) State five ways of preventing accidents caused by poor workshop keeping. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Rules/guidelines that control how work is done in the workshop to protect workers, customers, vehicles and the environment from injury or damage
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each (1 name + 1 protection): goggles/face shield - eyes from dust, sparks, paint; nose mask/respirator - lungs from dust and paint mist; ear defenders - hearing from noise of hammering/grinding; safety boots - feet from falling objects and sharp metal; gloves - hands from cuts, chemicals and heat; overall - body and clothing
5 marks: (c) Any five, 1 mark each: wipe up oil/water with sawdust or dry sand; keep gangways clear; return tools to racks after use; store paints and thinners in a fire-proof store; dispose of rags in metal bins with lids; good lighting and ventilation; label hazardous waste containers; report faulty equipment
questions.explanation: Safety rules are the guidelines that protect people and property in the shop. PPE: goggles (eyes), respirator (lungs), ear defenders (hearing), safety boots (feet), gloves (hands). Good housekeeping: absorb spills, clear gangways, store tools and flammables properly, use lidded bins for rags, keep the shop lit and ventilated, report faults.

questions.stem:
(a) Define oxy-acetylene welding. [2 marks]
(b) List five items of equipment that make up an oxy-acetylene welding set. [5 marks]
(c) Describe the three types of oxy-acetylene flame and state one use of each. [6 marks]
(d) State two safety precautions when lighting the torch. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A fusion welding process in which metals are melted and joined using the heat of a flame produced by burning acetylene in oxygen (with or without filler rod)
5 marks: (b) Any five, 1 mark each: oxygen cylinder; acetylene cylinder; regulators with gauges; hoses; blowpipe/torch; nozzles; flashback arrestors; spark lighter; goggles
6 marks: (c) Neutral - equal oxygen and acetylene, clear inner cone, for steel welding (2); carburising - excess acetylene, feather around the cone, for hard-facing/some non-ferrous work (2); oxidising - excess oxygen, short sharp cone, for brass/bronze (2)
2 marks: (d) Any two, 1 mark each: use a spark lighter not matches; open acetylene first and light it; point torch away from people and cylinders; wear tinted goggles; check for leaks before lighting
questions.explanation: Oxy-acetylene welding fuses metals with a flame of acetylene burning in oxygen. Equipment: two cylinders, regulators, hoses, blowpipe, nozzles, arrestors, lighter. Neutral flame (equal gases) for steel; carburising (excess acetylene, feather) for hard-facing; oxidising (excess oxygen) for brass. Light with a spark lighter, pointing away from people, wearing goggles.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between an integral body and a composite body. [4 marks]
(b) Describe the hammer-on-dolly and hammer-off-dolly methods of removing a dent. [6 marks]
(c) List five tools used in minor auto body repair. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Integral (monocoque): body shell and floor form a single welded load-bearing unit with no separate chassis (2); composite: body is built separately and bolted onto a separate chassis frame that carries the loads (2)
3 marks: (b) Hammer-on-dolly: dolly held directly behind the point struck; metal is squeezed between them, smoothing and stretching it
3 marks: (b) Hammer-off-dolly: dolly held under a low spot while the hammer strikes the high metal beside it; the high spot is lowered and the low spot raised with little stretching
5 marks: (c) Any five, 1 mark each: panel/planishing hammer; pick hammer; dollies; body spoons; pry bar; slide hammer/dent puller; body file; screwdrivers/spanners
questions.explanation: An integral body is a single load-carrying shell; a composite body sits on a separate frame. Hammer-on-dolly works directly over the dolly and stretches/smooths; hammer-off-dolly strikes beside the dolly to lower high spots while the dolly pushes up the low spot. Tools: hammers, dollies, spoons, pry bar, slide hammer, body file.

questions.stem:
(a) Name three types of spray gun and state how paint is fed in each. [6 marks]
(b) List five parts of a spray gun. [5 marks]
(c) State four precautions to observe when using a spray gun. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: (a) Gravity-feed - cup on top, paint flows down by gravity (2); siphon/suction-feed - cup below, paint drawn up by low pressure at the air cap (2); pressure-feed - paint forced from a separate pressurised pot or cup (2)
5 marks: (b) Any five, 1 mark each: air cap; fluid tip/nozzle; fluid needle; trigger; air valve; spreader (fan) control; fluid control knob; gun body/handle; cup
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: hold gun perpendicular at the correct distance; keep a steady speed and overlap strokes by about half; set the correct air pressure; never point the gun at anyone; clean the gun immediately after use; spray in a ventilated booth wearing a respirator
questions.explanation: Gravity (top cup), siphon (bottom cup, suction) and pressure-feed (separate pot) guns. Parts: air cap, fluid tip, needle, trigger, air valve, fan and fluid controls, body, cup. Precautions: correct distance and angle, 50% overlap, correct pressure, never aim at people, clean after use, spray in a booth with a respirator.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between thermoplastic and thermosetting plastics, giving one example of each. [4 marks]
(b) State four precautions when repairing plastic parts. [4 marks]
(c) Describe the steps in repairing a crack in a thermoplastic bumper by hot-air welding. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Thermoplastic softens/remelts each time it is heated, e.g. polypropylene, ABS, PVC (2); thermosetting sets permanently and does not remelt, e.g. polyester, epoxy (2)
4 marks: (b) Any four, 1 mark each: identify the plastic type first; avoid overheating which chars the plastic; work in a ventilated area as fumes are toxic; wear gloves and goggles; use a matching welding rod; keep heat away from fuel lines and wiring
7 marks: (c) 1 mark each step: identify plastic from moulded code; clean with soap and plastic cleaner; V-groove the crack; drill small holes at the ends of the crack to stop it spreading; tack and weld with hot-air gun and matching rod; allow to cool naturally; sand/shape flush and refinish with flexible primer
questions.explanation: Thermoplastics remelt (PP, ABS); thermosets do not (polyester, epoxy). Precautions: identify plastic, avoid overheating, ventilate, PPE, matching rod. Steps: identify, clean, V-groove, stop-drill ends, weld with hot air and rod, cool, sand and refinish.

questions.stem:
(a) State five factors to consider in locating an auto body repair workshop. [5 marks]
(b) List six items of tools or equipment needed to start a small auto body and spray painting shop. [6 marks]
(c) Explain two ways the owner can dispose of waste thinner and paint responsibly. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: (a) Any five, 1 mark each: capital available; accessibility/good road; cost and size of land; nearness to customers/market; electricity and water supply; security; government regulations/zoning; competition
6 marks: (b) Any six, 1 mark each: air compressor; spray guns; hammers and dollies; body jack; sanders/grinder; welding set; spray booth; tool kit of spanners; drilling machine
4 marks: (c) Any two, 2 marks each: use a solvent recovery unit to distil and reuse thinner; store waste in labelled sealed containers and hand over to licensed hazardous-waste collectors; never pour into drains or soil
questions.explanation: Location: capital, access, land, market, power and water, security, regulations. Equipment: compressor, spray guns, hammers/dollies, body jack, sanders, welding set, booth. Waste: recover solvent, store in labelled containers for licensed collectors, never pour into drains.
